currentState.summary: Signal separates state mutation from DeliveryQueue forwarding but set performs equality before the mutation lock and values snapshots before subscribing. Computed invokes combine while holding its latest-pair mutex and has construction windows. ViewModelActivator invokes active registration callbacks under its state mutex. DisposeBag, stream operators, DeliveryQueue bounds, and GPUI sender transport retain redundant ownership or clone work. Test Suite now exists and supersedes the old epic's Lab runtime plan.

decisions.title: Use one Signal commit boundary and a version-aware values handshake
decisions.decision: Keep equality, mutation, version assignment, and enqueue ownership under one Signal state commit boundary. Drain committed changes after releasing state. Register values against a captured value/version before the synchronous snapshot, buffer later versions during that callback, then deliver them in order without duplicate baseline delivery.
decisions.rationale: The direct state owner already owns value and version; extending that owner is smaller and safer than adding a scheduler or alternate stream type.

alternativesRejected.reason: This is the simplest current flow, but it preserves the lost-update window.
That adds scheduling semantics and complexity outside the existing Signal owner.

decisions.title: Build Computed from versioned source snapshots without locked user code
decisions.decision: Reuse the private version-aware Signal handshake for derive and combine2 construction. Clone the latest values under the Computed-owned mutex, release it, invoke user code, then replace the output Signal. Track source versions so construction skips only the captured baselines and retains every later commit.
decisions.rationale: This reuses the Signal invariant instead of introducing a second startup protocol and keeps user closures outside coordinator locks.

decisions.title: Use activation generation identity and dispose outside locks
decisions.decision: Publish one active generation bag and identity under the activator mutex, snapshot callbacks, release the mutex, then invoke callbacks. Tokens reference the generation they joined. Failure detaches only that generation and disposes outside the mutex. Store DisposeBag subscriptions directly in its mutex without an internal Arc.
decisions.rationale: Generation identity resolves the failure-versus-reactivation race while preserving the public reference-counted token contract.

alternativesRejected.alternative: Clone callbacks and keep count without generation identity
alternativesRejected.reason: It is smaller but cannot distinguish a failed generation from a later reactivation race.

controlFlow: Reserve or join a generation under lock.
On failure, detach only the matching generation and dispose outside lock.
On final matching token drop, detach and dispose once.
dataFlow: Callback registry + generation state -> callback bag -> Subscription disposal.
interfaces: ViewModelActivator, ActivatableViewModel, ActivationToken, DisposeBag, Disposable, and DisposeWith remain unchanged.
failureHandling: Callback error disposes partial work and returns the original error.
concurrencyAndTransactions: Generation count changes under one mutex.
Callbacks and disposal execute outside it.
DisposeBag keeps its own direct mutex and atomic disposed flag.
compatibilityAndMigration: A later generation is isolated from an earlier failed token.
observability: Callback counts and disposal counts are recorded by tests.
securityAndPrivacy: Generic values remain in-process; no persistence, network, credential, user identity, or new diagnostic payload boundary is introduced.
validation: Reentrant registration, concurrent activation, failure recovery, add/dispose race, and exactly-once disposal tests.

decisions.title: Remove only mechanically proven stream and delivery overhead
decisions.decision: Forward accepted filter values by their existing reference, remove filter and skip Clone bounds, own distinct and skip mutexes directly, remove DeliveryQueue::enqueue's unused Clone bound, retain filter_map and the subscriber-snapshot FIFO fanout algorithm, and make Signal forwarding direct.
decisions.rationale: Each change has direct clone-count, compile, or ownership evidence and avoids a speculative delivery redesign.

decisions.title: Own GPUI senders directly and notify through unit
decisions.decision: Capture futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedSender<V> directly in bind_stream_value. Implement notify_on with a unit channel so it neither clones nor transports V. Preserve the unbounded receive loop, foreground Context update, update-error termination, and GpuiBinding ownership.
decisions.rationale: The sender already supports shared sends through the existing callback ownership; Arc<Mutex> and notification payload transport enforce no additional invariant.
